title: PASK: Cold Start Mitigation for Inference with Proactive and Selective Kernel Loading on GPUs
problem: DNN inference suffers from significant cold-start latency when models are spawned from scratch (spot serving, serverless, edge computing), caused by kernel loading overhead where DL primitive libraries (cuDNN, MIOpen) prepare GPU code objects before execution.
motivation: Frequent start-stop inference scenarios (serverless, spot instances, edge) make cold-start kernel loading a critical bottleneck, adding 5–10× latency overhead to inference.
method: PASK loads GPU code ahead of time (while the GPU is computing earlier operations) rather than waiting until it's needed, eliminating delays from last-minute code loading. The system organizes GPU code by type in a cache, allowing it to reuse the same code across multiple layers of a neural network instead of reloading new code for each layer. By overlapping code loading with GPU computation, PASK keeps both the CPU and GPU busy, improving overall efficiency.
key_novelty: The core idea is to proactively load GPU code while the GPU is already computing, reusing applicable code across layers to avoid redundant loading work.
contributions: Proactive kernel loading strategy replacing reactive scheduling to interleave loading with computation
Categorical kernel cache organization for efficient kernel discovery and reuse
Selective kernel recycling across DNN operators to minimize new kernel invocations
5.62× average speedup on popular DNN models eliminating cold-start overhead
baselines: Existing DNN inference frameworks with reactive kernel scheduling
limitations: Evaluation limited to off-the-shelf GPUs; applicability to inference with dynamic shapes or custom kernels not fully discussed.
primary_theme: Proactive kernel loading to eliminate cold-start latency in GPU inference
